This  game is Great! Watching the trlr it certainly looked like it had potential but wasnt sure... Then i saw they had it for a big discount so i decided to pull the trigger & WOW! If you're an 80's kid who LOVED  the first few Alien movies the Lord Have Mercy did they get this So Right! The Music Perfect! The Look & Feel Perfect. I wish the sounds of the weapons came thru more as well as the reloading sound. Right out the gate you're Not confused about whats going on, you're Not confused about where to go who who to talk too. ALSO Playing with other chars who are ahead of you isnt you struggling to keep up while one  guy wipes the floor with everything that dare look at him crazy..... Ooooooh no you gotta work Together and fight as a team!  Or you will Fail which is awesome! Means you gotta Lock in and be Ready. The classes are pretty cool, they all have their own xp bars so if a friend wants to get in on round 2 or 3 you can just start a New Class with them no prob! There dont seem to be counters in the game maybe they will do that in 2 but there is Limited dodge roll so make sure to play around with dodging JUST with Movement....  Game has that Gritty Military feel with all the scratched metalic weapons you find that you can also paint and make it yours. The connecting with other players is easy, if you are not getting a match for the mission you are one then trying queing for the one you just did a lot of times the train behind you keeps moving forward & you can ride the wave. This game came outta nowhere for me but after leveling the demolisher some and the medic Im Excited to see what 2 will look like since its So Close to release!

Alien: Fireteam Elite stands out as one of the strongest cooperative experiences set in the Alien universe, and for me it represents the natural evolution of the franchise after Alien: Colonial Marines. If Colonial Marines delivered the best single‑player Alien campaign, Fireteam Elite confidently claims the crown for the best co‑op Alien game to date.

Atmosphere & World Design
The game nails the authentic Alien atmosphere from the very first mission. Every corridor, hive, and industrial complex feels ripped straight from the films — dark, oppressive, and alive with tension. The environmental storytelling is subtle but effective, reinforcing the sense that you’re fighting a losing battle against an overwhelming xenomorph infestation.

Characters & Classes
The playable classes are well‑defined and genuinely fun to experiment with. Each one brings unique abilities and tactical advantages, encouraging team synergy rather than chaotic shooting. The characters feel grounded in the universe, and the voice lines, animations, and combat roles contribute to a believable fireteam dynamic.

Weapons, Perks & Customization
One of the game’s strongest points is its weapon and perk customization system. Firearms feel weighty and satisfying, from pulse rifles to shotguns and smartguns. The perk grid (skill tree) is surprisingly deep, allowing players to tailor builds for damage, survivability, support, or utility. Modifying weapons and abilities becomes a core part of the progression loop, and it genuinely enhances replayability.

Combat & Mission Structure
Combat is fast, brutal, and relentless. The variety of xenomorph types keeps encounters dynamic, forcing players to adapt on the fly. Missions are well‑paced, with a good balance between defensive stand-offs, corridor pushes, and boss-like encounters. The map design supports both strategic positioning and chaotic firefights, making each run feel intense and cinematic.

Co‑Op Experience
This is where Fireteam Elite truly shines. The game is built around cooperation — not just three players shooting together, but three players thinking together. Coordinating abilities, covering angles, and reacting to swarms creates a thrilling rhythm that few co‑op shooters manage to achieve. It’s the closest thing to feeling like a Colonial Marines squad under siege.

Overall Impression
Alien: Fireteam Elite is one of the best titles in its genre: polished, atmospheric, and deeply respectful of the Alien legacy. It offers a robust progression system, satisfying combat, and a co‑op experience that feels both challenging and rewarding. After finishing it, I can confidently say I’m excited for Fireteam 2 — the potential for expanding classes, enemies, and narrative depth is enormous.
